title: Chili Mac Skillet
subtitle: Two cravings, one pan
description: Two cravings, one pan. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven
Hotel pans or large baking dishes

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chili Mac Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown ground beef with onion and bell pepper, breaking into fine crumbles. Drain excess grease — greasy chili mac separates on the line.

steps.title: Simmer the chili base
steps.instruction: Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, and oregano; cook 1 minute. Stir in tomato paste, diced tomatoes, beans, and beef broth. Simmer 20–25 minutes until thickened and flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Cook macaroni separately
steps.instruction: Boil elbow macaroni in salted water until just al dente. Drain well — starch makes the pot gluey if you cook pasta in the chili too long.

steps.title: Combine chili and mac
steps.instruction: Stir cooked macaroni into the chili pot until evenly coated. The mix should look saucy, not dry — add a splash of broth if needed.

steps.title: Melt cheese on top
steps.instruction: Top with shredded cheddar. Cover 2 minutes to melt, or broil 2–3 minutes for browned cheese edges. Keep the pot on low for seconds.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Chili Mac Skillet onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve Chili Mac Skillet
steps.instruction: Ladle into bowls or serve straight from the Dutch oven with sour cream and green onions on the side. This is chili AND mac — both should be obvious in every bite.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Serve straight from the Dutch oven or ladle into bowls — mac elbows should be visible in the chili.
Sour cream and green onions stay cold on the side.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Two cravings, one pan. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
